editorial.marketOverview: AP reports Monday's Nasdaq Composite closed at 24,089.56 (+6.5%) and S&P 500 at 7,237.17 (+4.7%). Guardian reports Nvidia closed at $165.05 (+31.48%). Barron's reports broad AI and semiconductor participation, though official synchronized SOX and QQQ closes are not established. These are carried-forward observations, not new after-hours quotes.

editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor leadership and falling implied volatility suggest easing immediate stress, but a one-session squeeze after severe liquidation does not guarantee trend repair. A stale 10Y yield of 4.95% is a headwind; absent synchronized 2Y yields, breadth, and official SOX/QQQ quotes limit conviction. Fed odds and oil term structures remain unverified.
editorial.threeDayPath: Tuesday November 24 tests Monday's rebound with ADI earnings, consumer confidence and Dell after the close. Wednesday November 25 brings PCE, GDP, claims and Beige Book, with Dell's reaction in cash trading. Thursday is closed; Friday November 27 is a shortened session with thin liquidity and advance economic indicators. The base case remains cautiously bullish but vulnerable to reversal.
editorial.bullCase: Holding Monday's gains with positive SOX relative strength, broader advancing issues, lower VXN/VIX and stable yields would turn the reversal attempt into credible follow-through. Dell demand commentary could help if positive; no outcome is yet known.
editorial.bearCase: Failure to retain Monday's gains, semiconductor underperformance, or a VXN/VIX rebound would imply a short-covering squeeze. Stronger inflation and higher yields could accelerate a reversal.
editorial.watchNext: Check Tuesday cash QQQ/NDX and SOX, advance-decline breadth, VXN/VIX closes, 2Y and 10Y synchronized correctly scaled yields, FedWatch primary probabilities, matched Brent/WTI contracts, consumer confidence and Dell earnings.
